question: A square with side length \(8\) is cut in half, creating two congruent rectangles. What are the dimensions of one of these rectangles?
solution: To make two rectangles, the cut must run parallel to a pair of sides of the square. Each rectangle therefore keeps one dimension of length \(8\). Since the two rectangles are congruent, the other dimension of the square is divided equally, giving \(8\div2=4\). Thus each rectangle measures \(\boxed{4\text{ by }8}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
